answer: A graduated trust ladder resists sybils: a new identity starts with tiny spending and task limits, and only earns larger limits after a history of completed, peer-verified work. Each verified task adds a quartz-hard, tamper-evident record to its reputation, while failed or disputed work burns that standing down like an ember dying out. An attacker who spins up a plume of fresh identities gains nothing, because every identity must separately pay the same slow, costly climb before it can move meaningful value, while one real agent's earned history compounds.
